title: Stability of a complete field can be tested on separable extensions
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] complete for a nontrivial real-valued multiplicative nonarchimedean absolute value. Equip each finite field extension $E/K$ with its minimal-polynomial spectral norm $s_{E/K}$ [lem-trf-incomplete-spectral-algebra-norm]. Then $K$ is stable [def-trf-stable-nonarchimedean-field] if and only if every finite separable extension $E/K$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] admits a $K$-basis $e_1,\ldots,e_n$ such that $$s_{E/K}\left(\sum_i a_i e_i\right)=\max_i|a_i|s_{E/K}(e_i)\qquad(a_i\in K).$$ The stability conclusion includes all finite extensions, including inseparable ones.

source.place: Proposition 3.6.2/2, printed pp.157-158; used at the start of the ascent proof of Proposition 3.6.2/3 Local archival copy absent; WANTED in report.

proof.text: If $K$ is stable, its defining orthogonal-basis property applies to every finite field extension, hence in particular to the finite separable ones. This proves the forward implication.

Conversely assume the stated property for finite separable extensions. Choose an algebraic closure $\Omega/K$. Its spectral norm is a multiplicative nonarchimedean absolute value extending that of $K$, so $\Omega$ is a normed $K$-vector space. The subfield $K_s$ of separable algebraic elements is a separable closure of $K$ and is dense in $\Omega$ by the spectral-density lemma.

For a finite-dimensional $K$-subspace $U\subseteq K_s$, choose a finite basis. The filtered-union description of a separable closure puts these finitely many elements in one finite separable subextension $L/K$ of $K_s$. Its spectral norm is the restriction of $s_{\Omega/K}$: the monic minimal polynomial of an element over $K$ is unchanged by the inclusion. By the assumption $L$ has an orthogonal $K$-basis, and the cartesian-subspace lemma gives one for $U$ with its restricted norm. This includes $U=0$.

source.place: Proposition 3.6.2/2, proof, last sentence, finite-subextension interpretation of cartesianness

proof.text: Apply dense cartesian permanence with $V=\Omega$, $W=K_s$ and $N=s_{\Omega/K}$. The base field is complete, density is Step 2, and the required orthogonality on finite subspaces of $W$ is Step 3. Thus every finite-dimensional $K$-subspace of $\Omega$ has an orthogonal basis.

Let $E/K$ now be any finite extension, with no separability assumption. Choose an algebraic closure $\Omega_E$ of $E$. Algebraic-closure equivalence for the algebraic extension $E/K$ gives a $K$-isomorphism $\Omega_E\simeq\Omega$ and hence an embedding $j:E\hookrightarrow\Omega$. For every $z\in E$, injectivity gives $p(j(z))=0$ exactly when $p(z)=0$ for $p\in K[T]$; consequently the monic minimal polynomials, and their spectral coefficient formulas, agree. Thus $j$ is a $K$-linear isometry. Apply Step 4 to the finite-dimensional subspace $j(E)$ and pull its basis back along $j$. This gives the defining orthogonality formula for $E$, so $K$ is stable.

source.place: Proposition 3.6.2/2, proof, conclusion from cartesianness of the algebraic closure

The source (BGR 3.6.2/2, 3.4.1/6, 2.4.3/8) is not in literature/: it is WANTED and the proof is marked agent-written, so I checked the mathematics myself and could not compare against the page. The statement is unchanged and correct, and it covers inseparable E. Step 1 is an elementary specialisation of def-trf-stable-nonarchimedean-field. Step 2: lem-trf-spectral-norm-algebraic-extension needs a complete, nontrivial base, which holds, and gives a multiplicative norm on Omega; relative-separable-closure makes K_s a separable closure; density comes from the new node. Step 3: the finite basis lies in one finite separable L (def-pd-separable-closure), whose spectral norm is the restriction of s_Omega (same minimal polynomial; the two formulas differ only by reindexing). The hypothesis gives L an orthogonal basis and lem-trf-cartesian-subspace passes it to U, U=0 included. Step 4: every hypothesis of permanence holds (K complete, N an ultrametric definite homogeneous norm, W dense, step 3). Step 5: IsAlgClosure.equivOfAlgebraic gives a K-embedding E→Omega that is an isometry; pulling back the basis gives stability. New node separable-closure-spectral-density is true: for inseparable x, P+εT is separable with a root y where s(x−y)≤(|ε|s(x))^{1/d}. It is not a duplicate; lem-trf-separable-monic-approximation plus lem-sfb-roots-coefficient-proximity is a route for its proof. New node dense-cartesian-permanence is true: norm equivalence over complete K, approximation, then an isometry onto a subspace of W. The same argument appears inline only in lem-trf-completed-algebraic-closure-cartesian steps 6–8, not as a node, so it is not a duplicate. Neither new node restates a clause of the item. Form: statement-only, single backslashes, correct created/blueprint/unit fields; lean_audit is omitted, as in other landed trf nodes. The declared tool use of def-pd-separable-closure is a definition, which is harmless; I accept it. No fixes.
